title: Why Bees Die When They Sting

sections.name: Why Bees Die When They Sting
lines: When a honeybee stings you, it gives up its life to do it.
Her stinger is covered in tiny backward barbs, like a harpoon.
In your skin, the barbs hook in. So when she flies off, the stinger rips out of her body.
Its venom sac stays attached, and keeps pumping venom into you.
That's why you should get it out fast. Scrape it off with a fingernail or a card.
For most people, the pain and swelling fade within a day or so.
But wasps have smooth stingers. So they can sting again, and again.
